title: Public structural polynomial API
objective: Wire reviewed ordinary structural calculus and generated FLINT adapters into the public ZZ[x], QQ[x], and packed word-prime GF(p)[x] Polynomial API with correct portable fallback, lifecycle, Sage semantics, native selection, and performance.

handoff.summary: Adds public same-parent composition, reverse, signed shifts, truncation, integral, resultant, and discriminant for dense univariate polynomials over ZZ, QQ, and packed word-prime GF(p). Exact Node polynomials remain sealed generated FLINT resources, prime-field calls cross one packed UInt64 boundary, rational scalar resources close deterministically, and portable hosts use the reviewed ordinary structural calculus. The dispatch lives in a strict lazy module so the arithmetic bootstrap stays within budget. The focused witness forbids exact coefficient materialization and runs with normal and native-disabled execution. Warm Linux x64 medians were 0.79 ms for degree-64-by-8 ZZ composition, 0.60 ms for the degree-64 ZZ resultant, 0.41 ms for degree-1000 QQ integration, 1.17 ms for degree-256-by-8 61-bit GF(p) composition, and 0.15 ms for the degree-256 GF(p) resultant.
risks: The generated structural FLINT wrappers currently execute through the safe dynamic FFI path because structural_flint is not yet selected as a production compiled kernel; making that shared selection is intentionally left to the integration lane.

Linux x64 is validated locally. Portable tests prove the storage-neutral fallback infrastructure, but Linux arm64, macOS arm64, Windows fallback, and browser/WASM execution still rely on their normal CI lanes.

The repository-wide test:changed gate reached two unrelated inherited failures: compiler/algebra.py exceeded its fixture timeout, and compiler/matrix.py could not load the already-tracked lazy matrix_selection_public module from the standalone compiler fixture. All claimed focused, architecture, strict, and portable gates pass.
next_steps: Have the integration lane decide whether structural_flint should become a production compiled kernel after comparing compiled and generated dynamic-FFI startup and steady-state costs.
Add these public operations to cross-platform and browser polynomial differential matrices as the corresponding FLINT/WASM adapter coverage lands.
Extend the same lazy public-dispatch pattern to the remaining reviewed polynomial algorithms without growing the arithmetic bootstrap.
